title: Private deploy: Offline artifact sync, port rules, and upgrade acceptance criteria
creator: Sofia Martinez
summary: Define clear requirements and acceptance criteria for private/VPC deployments that must operate with restricted egress or fully air-gapped networks. Focus areas: deterministic offline artifact synchronization (image bundles & manifests), explicit port/ACL rules for runtime and control-plane components, and an upgrade path that supports rollback without external package pulls.
background: Several enterprise customers have requested an end-to-end private install experience where clusters can be provisioned and upgraded without outbound internet access. Existing acceptance artifacts focus on networking and offline upgrades independently; this ticket consolidates requirements for artifact sync mechanics (how packages are delivered and verified), port-level policies required for normal operation and optional diagnostic windows, and a validated upgrade/rollback flow suitable for air-gapped or highly restricted VPCs.
goals: Produce an acceptance checklist for offline artifact bundles (format, signing, manifest validation, deltas) that QA and customer ops can use
Declare a minimal set of inbound/outbound port and ACL rules for Private control plane and runtime components, with explicit optional ports for diagnostics
Define an upgrade/rollback playbook that works without external egress and includes verification gates and timed fallbacks
Ensure key management and image verification requirements are compatible with customer KMS/HSM offline key import patterns
out_of_scope: Designing a new artifact distribution service (we will accept tarball/OCI bundle standards)
Onboarding automation for every distro/version of customer OS images (we will provide docs and scripts for common platforms)
Runbook automation for third-party VPN setup — we'll document recommended patterns but not implement VPNs ourselves
requirements: Artifact bundle format: Support signed OCI-style bundles or gzipped tar bundles containing images, Helm charts, and a top-level manifest.json with checksums and semantic versioning
Signing & verification: All bundles must be signed using customers' PGP or X.509 keys; server-side verification must reject mismatched signatures and produce clear error codes

Delta upgrades: Bundles should support a delta manifest so upgrades can avoid full-image transfer where possible; acceptance considers delta-based verification successful if checksums and version lineage match

Port & ACL baseline: Document minimum required ports for normal operation (e.g., 443/tcp for control plane web UI if exposed internally, 8443/tcp for internal API, 10250/tcp kubelet where applicable, 50051/tcp gRPC for runtime apis) and specify that all others must be optional and gated by a configurable diagnostic mode
Offline KMS flow: Support importable key blobs and an explicit manual key rotation procedure; automatic external KMS calls must be optionally disabled
Upgrade orchestration: The upgrade controller must be able to perform image swaps, schema migrations, and KV cache rebuilds using only local artifacts and must expose a dry-run validation step

Rollback criteria: Define automatic rollback triggers (failed health probes beyond threshold, unacceptable latency regression, missing manifest artifacts) and ensure rollback can roll back both application code and schema/state changes where safe

Operational visibility: Runtime must emit audit-ready logs and a preflight upgrade report (checksums, node readiness, disk usage) to a local artifact so customers can collect it without remote telemetry
Deterministic install: Install-time checks must verify network policies, port reachability (internal control-plane endpoints), and local image integrity before marking the cluster healthy
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer-provided signed bundle and no outbound internet, an install using the documented procedure completes with all services healthy and a generated install report matching bundle checksums
Given a simulated restricted VPC with only the documented ports open, the product functions end-to-end (control plane, runtime, health checks) for normal inference workloads

An upgrade executed with a local delta bundle completes within expected time and, on verification failure, triggers an automated rollback to the previous known-good state without requiring internet access
Security checks: signature verification failures produce non-ambiguous errors, do not partially apply changes, and emit guidance to operators in the install logs
Key management: Customers can import key material via documented CLI steps and perform a rotation that the runtime accepts without contacting an external KMS
Telemetry and logs: The preflight and post-upgrade reports are produced in the specified local path; a manual operator following the runbook can validate success using only on-prem assets
Documentation: A README and runbook covering the bundle creation, bundle verification, step-by-step offline install, and rollback playbook are present in the release artifacts
test_plan: Create CI job that runs an end-to-end scenario in a controlled VPC with egress blocked: (1) generate signed bundle from CI artifacts; (2) run install on ephemeral VMs with only allowed ports; (3) exercise a small inference workload; (4) apply delta upgrade bundle; (5) intentionally corrupt bundle signature to assert failure behavior. Test should generate preflight and upgrade reports that are archived to the CI artifact store.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal verification in QA (2 weeks). Stage 2: Pilot with 2 enterprise customers who requested offline installs (coordinated windows). Stage 3: Documentation and release to general private deploy customers after pilot feedback. Each stage requires a sign-off checklist from security, reliability, and solutions engineering.
risks: Customers with heterogeneous OS images may see unexpected package dependency failures during offline installs
Large bundle sizes can cause slow transfer and storage constraints in low-bandwidth environments
Manual key import workflows increase operator burden and risk of misconfiguration
Rollback may not be fully reversible if customers perform custom, incompatible schema changes between releases
mitigations: Provide bundle creation tooling that includes a dependency checker and optional compression/diff generation
Recommend and document transfer strategies (s3 presigned -> air-gapped USB, rsync over secure link) and provide sample checksums for partial verification
Supply a validated key-import CLI and sanity checks that refuse weak key formats; include a recovery path description
Document explicit compatibility guarantees and make breaking changes opt-in with migration helpers
open_questions: Do customers require support for both PGP and X.509 signing out of the box, or can we prioritize one for MVP?
What maximum bundle size and transfer time do we certify for (this will affect acceptance thresholds)?
Should we offer an optional lightweight proxy appliance that performs authenticated bundle caching for multiple air-gapped clusters?
